items.title: Order an iPhone Duo now, and you'll probably get it before Christmas
items.content_html:
After iPhone Duo order dates slipped to the end of January 2027, Apple has brought them all forward, meaning they could now arrive before the holidays.

Online pre-orders for the iPhone Duo sold out instantly, and stocks were depleted almost as quickly at retail Apple Stores. There was some slight improvement after a couple of weeks, but now there is much more.

Ordering the iPhone Duo now in either color and with any of its storage capacities, gets a quoted shipping date of December 17-28, 2026. It's tight for Christmas Day, but it's hugely better than the previous estimate of January 26, 2027.

Buyers who had already ordered are also being told that their delivery dates have been brought forward significantly. One buyer told AppleInsider that they had originally been quoted January 2027, but instead received their iPhone Duo on November 16, 2026.

There's not enough information, even anecdotally, to determine how soon existing pre-orders are likely to ship. But with new orders just about beating the holidays, it should presumably be that existing orders arrive first.

As yet, the online Apple Store is showing no availability for order pickup at any physical store. It's previously been reported that Apple was concentrating on getting the iPhone Duo into stores for launch day, though, so it's likely that it aims to increase Apple Store stocks.

How Apple is doing this

Despite Apple saying that the demand for the iPhone Duo had been extraordinary, it has not and will not release figures. So it's not clear how many were even available at launch, and persistent rumors claimed supplies were limited because of production problems.

The date is still very close if you want to buy someone an iPhone Duo for the holidays, but it's a lot better than it has been.

There were then a pair of reports claiming that Apple was increasing production of the iPhone Duo. However, one was based on increased orders for components at certain manufacturers, and so ignored how Apple often switches suppliers.

The other specified that Apple had increased iPhone Duo orders by 30%. It made the same error conflating components with finished iPhones, but it was also based in part on some very dubious math.

Nonetheless, whether Apple has increased production or has just rectified manufacturing problems, it has now cut about a month off its previous delivery schedule.

items.title: Keychron K2 Ultra 8K review: More affordable 8KHz polling & custom RGB
items.content_html:
Keychron makes a lot of keyboards, but the latest Ultra 8K line is the peak of their offering, while the K2 keeps those specs and premium design affordable.

I'll be honest, I had to comb through the specs page to understand exactly what was different about the Keychron K2 Ultra 8K versus the Q1 Ultra 8K I reviewed recently. That's a compliment considering this keyboard is half the price.

When shopping for Keychron keyboards, it is best to understand what each portion of the name represents. In this case, the K2 is a step down from the Q-series thanks to its metal frame versus full-metal body, plus some other small differences.

The Ultra 8K moniker refers to the 8,000 Hz polling rate, long battery life, and the powerful MCU chipset. It's a performant keyboard that can be customized top to bottom.

If you're looking for the best of Keychron, an Ultra 8K model is it, though you can get it at a much more reasonable price with the K2 series. Let's get into the details.

Keychron K2 Ultra 8K review: Design

Keychron has a signature design that becomes difficult to differentiate without being an expert on the product lines. The K2 Ultra 8K is a 75% layout keyboard with Apex red, brown, or banana switches.

I chose the Apex red switches and was also able to test the K8 Ultra 8K, though it is nearly identical besides the few extra keys. Between the two, I prefer the smaller layout that weighs less at 2.39 pounds.

The K lineup lacks a volume knob, which isn't ideal since that has proven to be a very useful option. Even so, the F keys still work for volume and such on iPad and Mac.

I've learned to love the south-facing RGB backlighting, which can be fully customized with Keychron Launcher. Colors can be assigned to glow on a per-key basis but there's also the several presets and animations built-in.

The keycaps themselves are quite boring. They're available in this dull gray color scheme with a green escape key, though they can be swapped with key caps of your choice.

I would love to see Keychron try out keycaps with passthrough letters.

The design is nothing flashy beyond the RGB backlighting. It's fairly standard for Keychron and will fit in anywhere.

The Apex red switches I tested have a nice clack but they're not loud. There's also more than enough foam to keep the reverb low.

The feedback is also pleasant as each key depresses with and returns easily. I never feel fatigue when typing with these switches and they remain my go-to.

As with any mechanical keyboard, there are many layers here:

  • Double-shot PBT keycaps
  • CNC-machined aluminum frame
  • Apex red, brown, or banana switches; hot swappable
  • Steel plate
  • EVA Foam
  • IXPE Foam and PET Film
  • PCB
  • EPDM Foam
  • Bottom case PET Film
  • Silicone bottom pad
  • ABS bottom case

The reduced price and weight comes down to build materials compared to other keyboards. Keychron's Q1 line, for example, has a full metal body.

Keychron K2 Ultra 8K review: Features

One of the most interesting aspects of covering Keychron over the years is the incredible battery life gains. The K2 Ultra 8K has up to 760 hours of backlight-off use.

My current desktop setup minimizes wires so my keyboard is wireless. I'll eventually get a dock and some wires in here, but that day isn't today.

The Keychron K2 Ultra 8K lasts through days of work before needing a charge. Having the K2 and K8 to test has been handy, as I just swap them out as needed (this is silly, don't do this).

Some of these advanced specs are a bit lost on me, but they're great if you need them. The 8,000 Hz polling rate means you'll never run into timing issues when gaming.

Connect to your Mac, iPad, or PC through a 2.4GHz dongle, Bluetooth 5.2, or wired connection. By using the switch on the side and three Bluetooth radios, you can easily swap between five devices without un-pairing or re-pairing a device.

My setup is complex, as I can easily be using or testing several products at once. The Keychron K2 Ultra 8K lets me easily swap between the 2.4GHz connection to my Mac and the Bluetooth connections to my Apple Vision Pro and iPad.

All of these features are powered by the Keychron MCU with 1MB flash. Connect to a Mac or PC and visit the Keychron Launcher to customize every keypress and even each RGB LED.

Do be sure to visit the customization software and toggle on the 8KHz setting. All Keychron 8K keyboards ship with 1KHz on by default to ensure the widest compatibility.

If I had a complaint about how the Keychron system works, it's that I can't do any customization on the iPad. I'd love to see Keychron Launcher work via an iPad app since I'm sure it'll never work in Safari.

Using the Keychron K2 Ultra 8K

I've enjoyed using the Keychron K2 Ultra 8K these past several weeks, though I'm ready to get back to premium metals and knobs. The K2 series was the first mechanical keyboard I ever reviewed, and I still find it a perfect entry point into the hobby.

Keychron keyboards are incredibly consistent, and after years of using different models, I've never encountered more than the occasional bug. Lately, I've noticed that sometimes the keyboards are slow to wake from sleep mode, which can usually be fixed by toggling the power switch or connecting a cable.

Beyond that hiccup, I have zero issues.

My desk setup looks and feels great with a big mechanical keyboard at its center. The feet in the back let me raise the rear enough to ensure I'm at a comfortable typing angle too.

Uncompromised affordability

As I said at the top, I had to squint at the spec list to make sure I understood exactly why the K2 was half the price of the Q1. It comes down to build materials and switch options, but still.

At this price, the K2 Ultra 8K is a great option and hands-down a better option than Apple's Magic Keyboard. Sure, it's huge and heavy by comparison, but I'm not talking about it from a portability standpoint.

There's really not much else I can say that I haven't said in many previous Keychron reviews. These are some solid keyboards and I'll be the first to let you know if that ever changes.

If you want something a bit lighter and more affordable, I can easily recommend the Keychron K2 Ultra 8K.

Keychron K2 Ultra 8K review - Pros

  • Half the price and lighter than the premium Q1 model
  • South-facing RGB are bright and incredibly customizable
  • Hot-swappable switches, custom software, and a good typing experience
  • Connect up to 5 devices at once
  • Up to 760 hours of battery

Keychron K2 Ultra 8K review - Cons

  • No knob option
  • Lack of pre-configured color options
  • Would be nice if Keychron Launcher worked on iPad

Rating 4 out of 5

Since we have to give a numeric score, I can only say that Keychron continues to make almost perfect keyboards. They're expensive, and perhaps a little overkill for some, but they are great products.

Where to buy the Keychron K2 Ultra 8K

Get the Keychron K2 Ultra 8K mechanical keyboard from the Keychron website or Amazon for $119.99. It is only available fully assembled in black, though you get to choose between the Apex red, brown, or banana switch.

items.title: macOS 27.3 beta 2 lets you limit what AI automation apps can see and do
items.content_html:
Full Disk Access in Apple's macOS 27.3 gives users tools to clamp down on what AI automation tools can access. Here's what's restricted.

On Monday, weeks after the arrival of the PROLED MacBook Pro, Apple made macOS 27.3 developer beta 2 available for download. The software aims to improve user safety and data protection through changes to system settings regarding third-party apps.

The previous Device Control and Data Access option has been split into two settings: System & App Protection Override, and Accessibility. The former handles permissions for assistive apps by using entitlements, while the latter offers settings for apps that enable automation.

To be more specific, System & App Protection Override lets users choose which apps can utilize select apps or aspects of macOS to perform tasks. This setting will include guidance encouraging users to grant access only to apps necessary for their workflow.

Simply put, instead of giving an AI automation app access to your entire disk, you will now be able to limit access to just one or two apps of your choosing. Similarly, you can also limit the folders AI automation apps can access.

Why Apple added these settings

With Full Disk Access on macOS 27.2.1 and earlier, Apple didn't offer these granular options, meaning users could give apps access to their entire macOS disk. Apple has acknowledged the potential for improvement in that regard, particularly the need for warnings regarding the use of Full Disk Access.

"Before granting an app such extraordinary access, users should understand that it puts all of the data on their Mac at risk," says Apple's website. "These changes are designed to help them do that and to empower them to make informed decisions about their own data and privacy."

Apple has thus included warnings that explain the wide range of data apps can access and control if users enable full permissions. Users will also be able to make apps ask every time they require access.

Additionally, macOS 27.3 beta 2 adds a new transparency Menu Bar indicator, meant to make it more obvious when one app is controlling another with System & App Protection Override. It's a great security measure, given the ever-increasing prominence of AI.

Developers will need to prepare

Full Disk Access itself, meanwhile, won't be replaced. Apps that were already granted access will not lose it after updating to macOS 27.3, and the capability itself will continue to be available alongside the new security settings.

Developers may need to update their apps to ensure compatibility with the new macOS settings.

However, Apple has warned developers that they might have to update their apps to ensure they work properly with the new macOS Golden Gate settings. "Developers should be prepared to adjust how they onboard users and make sure their apps can gracefully handle having access to only a limited set of folders or apps," reads Apple's website.

Overall, these macOS enhancements will prove useful for anyone who relies on AI automation applications. Thanks to Apple's continued focus on user privacy and data security, you will no longer have to worry about apps trying to steal your data by simply asking for Full Disk Access.

items.title: Apple's face unlock for iPhone Duo works well, avoids Android's issues
items.content_html:
The main complaint about iPhone Duo is the lack of Face ID and the convenience it offers, so Apple has introduced a less secure face recognition option that can't be tricked with a photo.

When Apple introduced Face ID, it showed off how even complex Hollywood masks couldn't fool the system thanks to proof-of-life algorithms. Android smartphones have offered face recognition for years, but many were easily fooled by a 2D photograph.

Thanks to the highly insecure nature of face recognition that doesn't rely on infrared dot scattering and 3D mapping, it seemed Apple would never implement it. Then, as it started pushing for more advanced systems powered by Secure Exclaves, the feature popped up in Apple HomeView and then was added to iPhone Duo.

While it hasn't been confirmed whether face recognition is being powered by the Secure Exclave in iPhone Duo, it seems likely. The system appears to be much more advanced than simple AI facial recognition and image matching software.

iPhone 18 Pro already uses images in the Secure Exclave to help supplement it's under-display Face ID.

Subscribe to AppleInsider on YouTube

Apple is incredibly concerned with how secure its devices can be, so much so it took a global pandemic for it to use Apple Watch as a fallback option. An advanced version of Apple Watch unlock was introduced for iPhone Duo, seemingly based around the unlock mechanism used for Apple Watch on Mac.

The thinking there was that since Apple Watch was always authenticated as long as it remained on the wrist, it could serve as a different authentication tool on iPhone. It works great and can sometimes be faster than even Face ID, but it requires always wearing an Apple Watch.

Users complained that Touch ID felt like too much of a step down from Face ID. It seems Apple listened, though I'm not so sure that this wasn't always in the works and was simply pushed forward due to demand.

These kinds of features don't just appear overnight.

Anyway, face recognition is now an option for unlocking your iPhone Duo. Here's how that works and why you shouldn't worry about it being less secure than Face ID.

iPhone Duo face recognition setup and use

I already had Apple Watch unlock set up for my iPhone Duo and have had zero complaints. I always wear an Apple Watch, so I rarely find myself needing Touch ID outside of payment authentication.

Set up Unlock with Front Camera in Settings

Apple lets you use Apple Watch unlock alongside face recognition on iPhone Duo. It seems that the systems work together to determine which method should be used.

Toggle on Unlock with Front Camera by going to Settings, Touch ID & Passcode, then select the feature. It only works with the front camera likely due to resolution and fidelity.

The description reads as follows:

Use the front camera, along with a recent Touch ID or passcode authentication, to quickly unlock iPhone Duo when it's closed. Face recognition data never leaves your device. To use Apple Pay or to access your passwords, Touch ID is still required.

These three unlock features work independently of the other. The iPhone Duo looks to see if a finger is present on the Touch ID sensor, then, failing that, it unlocks with Apple Watch automatically.

If a face is in view, I notice it's a seemingly random chance on which unlock you're going to get. A little face appears in what is usually a thumbprint indicator when face unlock is used.

A little face indicator shows when face recognition is being used

You know which is used since the Apple Watch still taps you when unlocking via that method. I haven't tested it yet, but I would love to see the Apple Watch unlock feature fail if it sees a face that isn't mine trying to unlock the device.

It hasn't been a problem, but since turning on Unlock with Apple Watch and letting people try out my iPhone Duo, I've noticed it just unlocks for them. I'm right there and can see what they're doing, but I don't like that my device can unlock in their hands.

I plan to keep all three methods of unlocking turned on, as I don't really fear any of them leading to a security event. Apple seems to have really thought through the system to ensure it is secure.

The concern with face recognition

Apple users, especially the nerds that care enough to compare Android smartphones, have spent years making fun of the travesty that is face recognition unlock on Android devices. Security researchers have found that as many as 72% of the hundreds of devices they tested would unlock with a 2D photo.

Apple's Secure Exclaves help keep recognition and analysis data separate from the OS

That research was updated in 2026 to show a slight drop down to 63%, but the situation on Android is still dire. From my testing so far, Apple's implementation seems foolproof when it comes to photos or videos.

I expect that there's a very big difference in execution that allows one to be better than the other. Apple already has a ton of security built into its devices that Android manufacturers don't bother with due to expense, but there are also performance considerations and new hardware.

The iPhone Duo has a Secure Exclave, which initially was used simply to control when microphone or camera indicators should be shown. By having those features controlled by a Secure Exclave, Apple could prevent software or hackers from attempting to turn off the privacy indicators.

The Secure Exclave has also been used in Apple Watch for Audio Intelligence and Apple HomeView for facial recognition. Focusing on HomeView, that device uses a rolling feed of footage that isn't technically recorded to determine who is using the device.

Siri Recaps show up on iPhone but are powered by Apple Watch

While Apple has yet to publish a paper on the iPhone Duo face recognition software, I expect that it is performing a similar action. Instead of simply capturing a 2D photo then comparing it to face data stored in the Secure Enclave, it is relying on live video and AI analysis.

I tried tricking the iPhone Duo into unlocking with various photos of me and a video of me looking at the camera and moving around. Neither worked.

In fact, when the face recognition failed, I was required to use Touch ID. There was no retry, even when showing my real face.

While I will wait for people to try and brute force the system with more sophisticated means, I expect they'll either fail or require incredible methods. As it stands now, I am confident in Apple's implementation in a way I was never able to be with Android's.

Face ID is coming in version 2

While some are calling this a stopgap measure until Face ID can debut in iPhone Duo 2, I'd like to counter that a bit. Sure, that is the case on paper, but most people that own the first iPhone Duo won't be running out for version 2 a year later.

Touch ID is less convenient but secure and easy to use

We're talking about a $2,000 smartphone at the starting price. People are leasing these devices over years and likely want to keep them for years after that.

Sure, a next-generation model is coming with Face ID, likely in 2027, but let's not forget that doesn't help the millions that already own iPhone Duo. This is an excellent feature that appears to be quite secure and convenient in one.

Yes, Face ID is more secure, but unless you're under threat of attack from sophisticated adversaries, I doubt you need to worry. Though, it would be nice if Apple could allow users to combine face recognition with Apple Watch Unlock as a kind of two-factor system.

You'll want all three methods turned on since face recognition does not occur on the inner camera. It's interesting how Apple has approached this, and I'm quite glad it's here.

Apple is expected to release iOS 27.3 to the public in December. The feature is available in beta today, but AppleInsider still strongly advises against installing beta OS on critical hardware.

items.title: New in iOS 27.3 beta 2: Front camera unlock, Siri AI in Safari, more
items.content_html:
Apple's iOS 27.3 is now on its second developer beta, adding new locking and unlocking options for iPhone Duo, new Siri features for Safari, and an update to Apple Podcasts.

On Monday, a week after the release of IOS 27.2.1, Apple made iOS 27.3 developer beta 2 available for download. The first developer beta of iOS 27.3 introduced vertical Safari tabs, Siri Recaps, Live Rewind, and a redesigned Health app, among other things.

iOS 27.3 beta 2 also brings new features and enhancements, some exclusive to Apple's recently released foldable, the iPhone Duo.

Close To Lock & Unlock with Front Camera on iPhone Duo

With Monday's developer beta, iPhone Duo users have gained the ability to lock their device simply by folding it. The feature can be found in the Settings app, under Display & Brightness.

Apple has also included a new way of unlocking the iPhone Duo, seemingly as a way of compensating for its lack of Face ID. After a recent unlock via Touch ID or passcode, iPhone Duo users will be able to unlock their device with the front camera when closed.

However, Touch ID or passcode authentication is still required for Apple Pay and for the Passwords app. Front camera unlocking is only available for 45 minutes after an iPhone Duo is unlocked via Touch ID or passcode.

The front camera unlock feature can be activated from the Settings app, under Touch ID & Passcode. It's not exactly Face ID, but the capability will come in handy for anyone who hasn't gotten used to the iPhone Duo.

Siri AI's new capabilities in Safari

With the second developer beta of iOS 27.3, Apple made Siri AI much more useful when used in Safari. The virtual assistant can now answer questions about on-screen pages and take actions accordingly.

For instance, when users are reading through a travel guide on Patagonia, they can ask Siri AI to make a list of things they need to pack, based on the webpage. Siri AI can also provide insights on restaurant menus by highlighting gluten-free items and other food items when asked to do so.

Video podcasts in the Apple TV app, News+ puzzle expansion

As part of the beta updates released on Monday, the Apple TV app has gained video podcasts. Though video podcasts launched with iOS 26.4, they were previously limited to the Apple Podcasts app.

Now, podcasts in video form will be available in the Apple TV app on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV 4K, and via CarPlay.

Apple News+ subscribers in Australia, meanwhile, have gained access to a daily quick crossword, crossword mini, and Sudoku, along with Apple original puzzles, Quartiles, and an Emoji Game. The Quartiles game lets users make words using the provided tiles, while Emoji Game requires that users complete the smallest possible number of moves.

UK subscribers will now be able to access a daily quick crossword, crossword mini, and Sudoku, while French-Canadian Apple News+ users will get Apple original puzzles, Quartiles, and Emoji Game.

Calendar UI tweaks for better usability

With Monday's developer beta, Apple made slight adjustments to the Calendar app and its user interface. The Search and event creation buttons were moved to the bottom of the screen, meaning that key Calendar features are now close together.

The Today button, meanwhile, has also been modified. It now displays the current day and date, rather than simply the word "Today."

In terms of purely aesthetic changes, Apple modified the way month names are displayed. The month name at the top of the screen is now centered, rather than to the left.

Automation, Full Disk Access changes with macOS 27.3 beta 2

For Mac users, the second developer beta of macOS 27.3 splits Device Control and Data Access into two settings. Accessibility handles permissions for assistive devices through the use of entitlements, while System and App Protection Override offers settings for apps that enable automation.

To be more specific, the latter setting lets users choose which apps can take control of select macOS aspects or apps to perform tasks. Users can also choose which macOS apps and capabilities will be available to automation-focused third-party applications.

There's even a new Menu Bar indicator, meant to make it more obvious when one app is using another, all with user permission. It's a great security measure, given the ever-increasing prominence of AI.

Full Disk Access, meanwhile, won't be replaced. Apps that were already granted access will not lose it after updating to macOS 27.3, and the capability itself will continue to be available alongside the new security settings.

These Mac enhancements will prove useful for anyone who relies on AI automation applications. macOS 27.3 beta 2 as a whole, however, doesn't look as though it adds much else.

As for iOS 27.3 beta 2, it includes a variety of changes, but most of them aren't particularly impressive. Siri's new capabilities in Safari are the most significant part of the update, though it still took Apple two years to get there.

items.title: Second developer betas of iOS 27.3, macOS 27.3 out for testing
items.content_html:
Apple has reached the second round of developer betas for iOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, and other operating systems in its software ecosystem.

The second round of the current generation of developer betas has arrived, enabling developers to see what's coming to the public release in December.

The second developer builds of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3 Golden Gate, watchOS 27.3, visionOS 27.3, and tvOS 27.3 surface after the first, which landed on November 3.

The second builds are:

  • iOS 27.3 beta 2 is 24C5049d, replacing 24C5037i
  • iPadOS 27.3 beta 2 is 24C5049d, replacing 24C5037i
  • macOS 27.3 beta 2 is 26C5047e, replacing 26C5035r
  • watchOS 27.3 beta 2 is 24S5296d, replacing 24S5284h
  • visionOS 27.3 beta 2 is 24N5298d, replacing 24N5286r
  • tvOS 27.3 beta 2 is 24K5298d, replacing 24K5286g

Other build numbers will be added as they become available.

At the same time, Apple has also introduced two update release candidates for older macOS versions:

  • macOS 26.7.4 RC 1 is 25G422
  • macOS 15.8.4 is 24H319

The first round introduced a number of changes in iOS 27.3, including vertical tabs an adaptive Dark Mode, and new Siri AI capabilities in Safari. The Health app also returned following a brief hiatus, while Apple Fitness+ gained Gym Strength.

For this second round, we do already know that there will be some video podcast changes for tvOS, with the addition of a new section in the second developer beta. Other alterations to video podcasts in the Podcasts app in general are also apparently on the way, but not necessarily in this update.

As always, AppleInsider warns readers not to use developer beta software on primary or mission-critical systems, unless absolutely necessary. Ideally, they should do so only with adequate backups of their data on hand, and ideally on secondary non-essential devices.

Over on macOS, the update introduced Live Activities to the Menu Bar.

Members of the public are usually better suited to trying out the public betas.

Find any changes in the new builds? Reach out to us on X at @AppleInsider or @Andrew_OSU, or send Andrew an email at andrew@appleinsider.com.

items.title: App Store hits 200,000 app milestone for iPhone Duo support
items.content_html:
There are now more than 200,000 apps made to work with the iPhone Duo, doubling the total in just ten days.

On November 6, Apple said that developers had managed to make over 100,000 apps work with the iPhone Duo and its dual-screen setup. It's not taken long, but that number has been doubled.

In an X post on November 16, Apple SVP of Marketing Greg Joswiak declared that over 200,000 apps are now optimized for the iPhone Duo.

Over 200,000 apps are now optimized for iPhone Duo! That number DOUBLED in just over a week.

I'm excited by how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and I can't wait to see what they build next.

— Greg Joswiak (@gregjoz) November 16, 2026

"I'm excited by how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and I can't wait to see what they build next," mused the executive.

Still early days

The number is certainly cause for celebration within Apple, as it means there's even more apps that will handle the iPhone Duo's environment properly. However, that figure does have to be considered carefully.

Having a pile of apps "optimized" for the iPhone Duo isn't the same thing as building from scratch. This also means developers adapting existing apps to work with the Duo's inner and outer displays.

While a small percentage will be apps made purely with the iPhone Duo in mind, many will simply be bolting on support to existing apps and uploading to the App Store, with little in the way of reworking the app.

items.title: Apple Pay chief Jennifer Bailey's successor is a longtime company veteran
items.content_html:
Apple has reportedly selected Corey Fugman as the new head of Apple Pay and Apple Wallet, taking over as his boss retires.

Jennifer Bailey is retiring as vice president of Internet Services and Apple Pay, after 23 years with the company. According to Bloomberg, her successor is to be Corey Fugman, who has followed a similar career path within Apple, but first joined 26 years ago.

Apple has not commented on the report and it is not known whether Fugman will take on all of Bailey's responsibilities. But he is said to be taking charge of Apple Pay, Apple Wallet, and also Apple Card.

This means he will oversee the completion of the move of Apple Card from Goldman Sachs to JPMorgan Chase. Bailey oversaw both the creation of Apple Card and the beginning of its move to JPMorgan Chase, but that move is not expected to complete until 2028.

Unnamed sources said to be familiar with the move say that Fugman has already been highly involved in the change to JPMorgan Chase. He was already a senior director of Apple Pay and Wallet, but will now be in direct charge of Apple's financial services.

Prior to being a senior director, Fugman started in Apple retail. That gives him a similar background to Bailey, who began her time at Apple by running its online retail operation.

While Fugman has not yet been officially announced, he is expected to report to Eddy Cue, Apple's senior vice president of services. Cue had previously told staff that Bailey's successor would be announced before the end of October 2026.

He also announced that Bailey would be continuing to advise Apple for an unspecified time after she steps down.

items.title: Siri AI daily usage limits and fees will launch with iOS 27.3
items.content_html:
Apple has unveiled its charges for users who utilize Siri AI more than a quite vague amount, and confirmed how the fees are tied to iCloud+ subscriptions.

As Apple has been saying since July 2026, Apple Intelligence compute costs are tied to iCloud+ subscriptions. The company has now revealed more of what those costs are, and how users will be kept informed of their usage.

Apple Intelligence and Siri AI does not depend on users paying for an iCloud+ subscription. All users will always be able to make the most simple requests such as sending a text message or setting an alarm.

Then all users will have the ability to use an unspecified number of more complex Siri AI requests. While Apple hasn't defined any particular number, these more complex requests are ones that require server-side handling rather than being done entirely on-device.

From iOS 27.3, Apple is imposing daily usage limits on such requests as Siri AI and image editing tools like Extend. There are also limits on Shortcuts and third-party apps that use Apple Foundation Models.

Using iCloud+

Apple's iCloud+ offers greater cloud storage and other benefits, which now include further AI requests in all but the lowest tier. Users on the lowest $1/month 50GB iCloud+ tier do not get any further usage allowance.

Beyond that, all tiers get increased AI usage:

  • 200GB tier ($2.99/month) has up to twice the regular limit
  • 2TB tier ($9.99/month) has up to five times
  • 6TB tier ($29.99/month) has up to ten times
  • 12TB tier ($59.99/month) has up to 20 times

What Apple is not making clear is precisely what these figures actually mean. The company is not saying how many Siri AI requests fall within the limits, for example, nor how many times Image Playground can be used.

Apple describes the regular daily usage limit as being per device. So presumably if you exceed the limit on your iPhone, you can try it on your iPad.

Previously finding out how much AI usage you've done has taken a couple of steps, but now from iOS 27.3 there will be notifications. Users will be notified when they hit around 80% of their limit, and the limit resets every 24 hours.

If a user hits their limit and needs to continue without waiting for the reset, the notification will include the option to pay to get more usage. However, this is not a one-time extra, it is not a way to increase the limit for the current day alone.

Instead, it is an upsell to the next tier of iCloud+. This means that users will then be on that next tier until they actively choose to change their plan back down to their previous tier.

There are no changes to the iCloud+ pricing tiers. And iCloud+ storage can be shared with your family, in which case the extra AI usage can be shared with them too.

Fans of Pokemon can celebrate their fandom in Japan by buying special edition Apple Gift Cards and playing Pokemon Go at Apple Stores.

Pokemon has managed to survive as a major gaming franchise for 30 years, and has fans all over the world, including at Apple retail. To mark the 30th anniversary, fans in Japan can now go to their local Apple Store for some extra festivities.

From November 16 until November 30, consumers can now pick up a Pokemon Special Edition Apple Gift Card. The cards can be used to make purchases on an Apple Account as usual, but are emblazoned with Pokemon imagery.

The cards are available at all 11 Apple Store locations in Japan, and can be loaded with any amount from 1,000 yen ($6.27) to 250,000 yen ($1,567) at the time of purchasing.

Supplies will also be limited, warns the official App Store Japan X account, with a maximum of three cards per customer.

Buyers won't just get the card. They can also scan a QR code on the back of the gift card to get three Pokemon-themed iPhone backgrounds.

Pokemon Go to the Apple Store

You don't have to pick up a gift card from the Apple Store to get in on the fun. Players of Pokemon Go can also take part in events at the stores.

Each store will become a PokeStop during the promotional period, with lures put out for players to use. The account hints that players could be lucky enough to encounter an "Applin," which is a grass dragon-type Pokemon.

At this time, it appears to be a promotion that is limited only to Japan, and not other regions.

Some stores will also hype the anniversary with in-store posters and big-screen images.

This is not the only Pokemon-related promotion under the Apple umbrella. In October, a collaboration resulted in the Beats Pill with Pikachu and Mimikyu art.

items.title: Oprah's 'Favorite things' giveaway just awarded $240,000 in iPhone Duos
items.content_html:
Oprah Winfrey surprised 120 caregivers with Apple's $1,999 iPhone Duo during her first live Favorite Things giveaway in 15 years, giving the new foldable iPhone a major celebrity endorsement just weeks after its launch.

The giveaway appeared in a November 12 episode of Oprah, celebrating the 30th anniversary of her annual Favorite Things tradition. The New York audience included nurses, hospice workers, emergency responders, and parents caring for children with special needs.

Winfrey organized the event to recognize people who spend much of their lives caring for others. The iPhone Duo appeared roughly 62 minutes into the 78-minute episode, drawing cheers and applause from the audience.

The device also earned a place on Oprah's 2026 list, where she highlighted its large folding display and compact design. Winfrey has been using the iPhone Duo herself since getting one.

It's not the first time Winfrey has singled out a major Apple product for her holiday audience.

Subscribe to AppleInsider on YouTube

In 2010, she called the original iPad her "No. 1 favorite thing ever" and gave away 275 tablets during an episode of The Oprah Winfrey Show. Her latest Favorite Things selection explicitly references that earlier endorsement, connecting Apple's first tablet with its first foldable iPhone.

Apple introduced the iPhone Duo in September and began selling it on October 23. Starting at $1,999, the device combines a 7.6-inch folding display with a smaller 5.4-inch exterior screen, allowing it to function as both a conventional phone and a larger-screen device.

The unusual design has attracted attention beyond its high price. Our iPhone Duo review praised the flexibility of its two displays, although questions remain about long-term durability and the compromises that come with a folding device.

Winfrey's endorsement gives Apple another opportunity to introduce the design to consumers who might not otherwise follow new technology releases. Her original iPad giveaway helped make Apple's tablet a holiday talking point, and the iPhone Duo now has a similar moment in the spotlight.

Apple has already acknowledged supply constraints for the iPhone Duo. CEO John Ternus said earlier in November that the company couldn't predict when production would catch up with demand.

items.title: Apple Music's Drake helped steer the unfilmable 'Neuromancer' to Apple TV
items.content_html:
Rapper Drake's production company is one of those behind the first-ever TV dramatization of William Gibson's said to be unfilmable "Neuromancer" novel, which debuts on Apple TV in January 2027.

Apple TV already has a reputation for high-budget science fiction series such as "For All Mankind" and "Silo." But because of "Foundation," it also has a reputation for attempting to make series out of science fiction that's previously been considered unfilmable.

That's the case again with "Neuromancer," which Apple TV greenlit back in February 2024. Now the producers behind the dramatization of William Gibson's famous novel say that Apple Music's Drake has been key to the production, and to it coming to Apple TV.

"Drake has always been a fan of 'Neuromancer' and as a storyteller has great taste, but that's only part of it," producer JD Dillard has now told Wired. "The real magic is that he's built an incredible team at his production company DreamCrew that he trusts to bring things to life once he identifies something he loves or believes in."

"Neuromancer" is being produced by DreamCrew along with Paramount Television Studios and Anonymous Content. The original novel is part of a trilogy by Gibson and the team has at least looked at dramatizing all three.

"It was kind of serendipitous that as Drake and DreamCrew had identified the books," continued Dillard, "all of these parties were starting to form and realize that they could work together to go get the rights."

"Drake, individually and by way of DreamCrew, is part of the mix and remains an important part of our process," he concludes.

Apple TV's contribution

There are no details of whether Dillard and fellow executive producer Graham Roland shopped the series around to various streamers. But as of 2024, Apple TV was on board and usually it takes a hands-off approach once it has decided to back a project.

That reportedly changes rapidly if Apple proves to be unhappy with the footage it's shown. But it's one reason that Ben Stiller has publicly praised Apple over producing "Severance" for the company.

In the case of "Neuromancer," Apple did have a suggestion.

"Apple had a great experience with Callum [Turner] on 'Masters of the Air'," said Roland, "and they encouraged us to meet with him."

"He was in LA for something else and he came to meet JD [Dillard] and I," continued Roland, "and within five minutes of hearing his voice it was like, 'this is the guy.'"

The first two episodes of "Neuromancer" debut on Apple TV on January 22, 2027. The remaining episodes stream on Fridays until March 19, 2027.

items.title: PSA: Beware of old Bitly links taking you to terrible sites
items.content_html:
Internet users really should be careful about link shortening services, as the recent spate of Bitly link hijacking affecting social media accounts demonstrates.

Link shortening services like Bitly are meant to be useful tools, enabling long URLs to be more manageable on social media, such as on X. However, it can also be an attack vector that will catch some users, and major brands, out.

Add in that browser scams tricking Mac users into bypassing Mac security protections is on the rise, and it becomes a really big problem.

Social media accounts for companies including McDonald's, Burger King, and even President Donald Trump, were showing posts with unexpected content changes. They included Bitly URLs that had been redirected to completely different content.

As collected by Cybernews, a McDonald's post from July 2011 suggested users could check out what its team in Sweden did that was "Pretty Cool." However, the preview of the Bitly link in X showed it went to the Wikipedia page for the September 11 attacks.

why would McDonald's Sweden do this https://t.co/zPLESwm4XK

— nyara (@nyaraVT) November 15, 2026

Similarly, a post from Burger King dated July 2011 proposed that readers could find their nearest restaurant via a Bitly link. The X preview showed it was a Wikipedia list of Nazi concentration camps.

Another early tweet from Trump talked about a "clubhouse on the North Sea," with the link going to a Wikipedia entry covering the Epstein Files.

None of the URLs would be anything the brands or Trump would openly link to in such a way. However, they all involve link shortening services and very old social media posts.

Online link rot

The problem is one involving how Bitly treats old links that the service handled. For some reason, not only was it possible for links to expire, but they could also be reused.

In an X post on the matter, posted on Sunday, Bitly admits it had to deal with an issue where "bad actors" were able to repurpose "certain old, inactive links" to send Internet users to other unrelated content.

Earlier today, we identified an issue that allowed bad actors to repurpose certain old, inactive links to redirect people to content unrelated to the original posts. We have suspended the accounts involved and are disabling the affected links. Our Trust and Safety team is working to address the issue and strengthen protections against similar misuse in the future.

— Bitly (@Bitly) November 15, 2026

Bitly insists it has suspended the accounts that did this, and is working to disable those affected links. It also says its Trust and Safety Team is working on the problem to prevent similar instances of link misuse.

Presumably one of the measures it will have to undertake is not expiring links in the first place.

Beware of Bitly

The affair has lessons for both sides of the link equation. For the moment it seems like a problem that pranksters have used to full effect, but it could easily have involved the spread of malware.

For those viewing the Bitly links on social media, carefully check the link preview before clicking it, if available. If there is an obvious disconnect between the account linking the content, the age of the post, and the preview, you probably shouldn't click it.

If you don't have a preview available, Bitly has a link checker, which you can paste a URL into to see the final destination. You could also add a plus symbol to the end of a Bitly URL to see the destination.

For people sharing links online, this serves as a reminder that using intermediary services like Bitly must be done with caution. You are handing over control of your links to another service which could be the victim of a breach or simply die overnight.

It's a trade-off, losing control in favor of a more easily shared URL. But, in cases like this, it's something that can eventually become a problem long in the future.

items.title: 'Schmigadoon!' and 'Widow's Bay' earn Grammy nominations for Apple
items.content_html:
The 2027 Grammy Awards nominations include one nod for recent Apple TV hit "Widow's Bay," and another for the show Apple cancelled, "Schmigadoon!"

Despite Apple TV cancelling "Schmigadoon!" after two seasons had aired — and a third had been written — the musical has gone on to greater success on stage. It has already won multiple Tony Awards, and now has been nominated for a Grammy.

The 2027 Grammy Award nominations have just been announced and include:

  • Best Musical Theater Album: Schmigadoon!
  • Best Score Soundtrack For Visual Media: Widow's Bay

Apple Music has already added a Grammys 2027 nomination playlist.

The "Schmigadoon!" stage musical is based in part on the first season of the Apple TV version. Back in June 2026 when it won Tony Awards including Best Musical, its producer called out the streamer for the cancellation decision.

"I think I should start by thanking Apple TV for cancelling the third season of 'Schmigadoon!' the TV show," said Christine Schwarzmann, "because without them we couldn't have picked it up and ran with it."

It's because of "Schmigadoon!" that Apple became an EGOT winner, the recipient of Emmys, Grammys, Oscars, and Tony Awards. But in September 2026, it was "Widow's Bay" that led Apple TV to record-breaking Emmy wins.

Those Emmys includied ones for Outstanding Music Composition and Outstanding Music Supervision. Now the show has been nominated for a Grammy for best soundtrack score.

The winners will be announced on Sunday, February 7, 2027. For the first time in 54 years, the Grammys will be screened on ABC.

items.title: Video Podcasts are coming soon to tvOS
items.content_html:
Apple is finally catching up with the trend of video podcasts, by adding a video podcasts section to the Apple TV in Monday's tvOS 27.3 developer beta.

Video podcasts have been growing in popularity in recent years, with both YouTube and Spotify hosting large numbers of them. Now, Apple wants to become a bigger presence in the market, including on Apple TV.

A video podcasts section will be added to the Apple TV on Monday, as part of the developer beta, reports the New York Times. The section will be available to all testers and will make it easier for users to watch that content.

This was a previously known change, with podcast updates previously revealed to be coming to tvOS 27 at some point.

It's not the only thing Apple has planned, as it apparently wants to increase the number of video podcasts shown in its Podcasts app.

The Podcasts app was updated earlier in 2026, with the addition of native video playback powered by HTTP Live Streaming, or HLS.

"We want podcasts to be available wherever people want to enjoy them - the small screens, big screens," said Apple VP Oliver Schusser who manages services including podcasts. The intention is claimed to be to help improve discovery for users, and for content creators to reach a new audience.

Schusser insists that it wasn't done in a way that would "financially benefit" Apple.
